summary: Batching-induced runtime crash-loop causing elevated 5xx waves across sync and streaming endpoints
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 06:20 UTC AstraPay observed elevated 5xx responses across sync generation and streaming sessions. Impact: customer-facing production traffic experienced ~18% 5xx rate for 30+ minutes, causing degraded user experience and retries. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-west (tenant astrapay-dedicated-01) running multiple pinned models. Observed both API 502/503 and runtime process exits. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and follow-up.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a mix of streaming and sync requests from a single tenant at high QPS (~350 rps) with long prompts (avg 600 tokens). 2) Confirm large batched requests from the router (batch_size ~64) to single runtime replica. 3) Observe runtime pod memory climb and crash loop within 6-12 minutes, followed by upstream 502/503 responses and connection resets to API gateway.
logs: Runtime stderr snippets: 'kv_cache_alloc: failed to reserve contiguous block', 'kernel_launch OOM on device 0', 'unhandled exception: segfault in attention kernel', kubelet logs: 'Container crashed - BackOff', api-gateway: 'upstream reset by peer (connection reset) 502', loadbalancer: '503 unhealthy upstream'. Traces: sample request id r-64215 shows initial streaming chunks then sudden FIN from runtime at token ~42.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: 1) Batch amplification combined with long sequences causes memory/fragmentation leading to kernel OOMs; 2) Autoscaler mis-inferred capacity, allowing a single replica to receive oversized batch fan-in; 3) KV cache eviction pathology on quantized models led to per-request spikes. Findings: - Correlated crash timestamps with tenant burst windows and high batch_size values from the router. - Kernel OOM logs present on runtime nodes followed by coredump files. - Autoscaler logs show scale decisions lagging behind ingress; scale-to-zero not implicated. - Canary with reduced batch_size (<=16) removed crash symptom. - Related PR changes to batching heuristics merged last week (see related_github_prs).
mitigation_actions:
Short-term: Implemented runtime-side guard to reject batches >32 tokens for pinned models in astrapay pool and configured API gateway to limit per-connection concurrent streams. Mid-term: Rolled back recent batching heuristic change in staging and pushed a fix that applies per-model max-batch constraints and fails fast on allocation errors (PR referenced). Autoscaler config tuned to add proactive buffer for tenant-dedicated pools.
Customer communication: Notified AstraPay CS contact at 2026-03-12 07:15 UTC with status updates and recommended immediate client-side backoff.
resolution: Root cause: A recent batching heuristic that favored large batch fan-in without per-model memory checks caused the serving runtime to allocate oversized device buffers for long-context requests on quantized kernels; this triggered kernel OOMs and process exits, producing upstream 5xx waves. What we changed: - Reverted aggressive fan-in heuristic. - Added per-model memory-aware batch caps and runtime alloc-fail fast path with clear 429/503 messaging. - Autoscaler safety buffer increased by 30% for dedicated tenants. The hotfix deployed 2026-03-12 10:40 UTC; system returned to normal error rates by 2026-03-12 11:05 UTC. Follow-ups: add automated test for batching memory feedback, include per-tenant burst-simulations in chaos tests, and schedule postmortem on 2026-03-16.
